racePreview.title: Sao Paulo GP
racePreview.headline: Champ Antonelli Hits Brazil as McLaren Unleashes  Upgrades
racePreview.summary: Kimi Antonelli arrives in Brazil as the F1 World Champion, while Mercedes chases the Constructors' title. McLaren brings major upgrades to the unpredictable Interlagos circuit.
racePreview.body:
Kimi Antonelli rolls into Sao Paulo as your new World Champion after locking up the title with a P3 in Mexico — pretty slick for the youngest champ ever, and he's even got a special Senna helmet for the occasion. Mercedes is looking to double down and clinch the Constructors' title here too, needing just three more points than Ferrari. Speaking of Ferrari, things got spicy in Mexico with Hamilton and Leclerc having a right old tangle and Fred Vasseur wasn't happy at all, calling it a "lack of respect" — not to mention George Russell bailing without a word to the media. Max Verstappen just snatched a win there, proving Red Bull are still seriously quick, bagging three of the last four victories.

Interlagos is a proper old-school circuit, a real driver's track with those elevation changes, heavy braking, and technical bits – plus, the weather can turn on a dime, with rain forecast for pretty much every day, especially Sunday, which could make things wild. McLaren's desperate to claw back third from Red Bull in the Constructors' and they're chucking a load of upgrades at the car this weekend, including new front and rear wings, hoping to regain that edge. This circuit really tests car balance, traction, and how teams manage their electrical energy under these 2026 regulations, so keep an eye on who masters that.

raceRecap.title: Sao Paulo GP
raceRecap.headline: Norris Masters Sao Paulo Chaos; Mercedes Crowned Champs!
raceRecap.summary: Interlagos delivered a chaotic wet-dry race, with Lando Norris taking a brilliant win. Max Verstappen surged from P21 to P2, and Mercedes clinched the Constructors' title.
raceRecap.body:
The 2026 Sao Paulo Grand Prix was an absolute classic, kicking off with a wild, rain-affected qualifying session that saw Lando Norris snatch pole, but also dished out grid penalties to half the field — seriously messing up the grid for Russell, Leclerc, Hamilton, and Verstappen. When the lights went out on Sunday, it was immediately clear it was going to be spicy, with Kimi Antonelli jumping Norris for the lead on intermediates. Things got even more dramatic as the track started to dry, and Lewis Hamilton gambled early on slicks, making up big ground. But then came the pit stop chaos: George Russell had a shocker, spinning his Mercedes on the pit exit. Antonelli's race also took a turn, with the championship leader spinning into Turn 1 on Lap 20, allowing Norris to reclaim the lead. Antonelli was heard on the radio reporting, "The car is pulling on one side when accelerating, it's so weird."

From there, Norris — who started from pole position after a dramatic qualifying — pretty much controlled the race, pulling out a solid gap. But the real story was Max Verstappen, who put on an absolute show. Starting way back in P21 due to engine penalties, he carved through the field like a hot knife through butter, eventually securing an insane second place. Isack Hadjar also had a stellar drive, rounding out the podium for Red Bull, making it a double podium for them. Meanwhile, with Russell finishing P4 and Antonelli P5, Mercedes locked up the Constructors' Championship — a massive result for them. Although Antonelli is under investigation for an unsafe release, his P5 finish was well clear of Oscar Piastri, so his position is safe.
